summary: This Snowflake documentation page describes the CREATE EXTERNAL FUNCTION command, which creates a function that calls a remote service through a proxy service such as Amazon API Gateway or Azure API Management. It covers the syntax, required parameters (name, arguments, RETURNS, API_INTEGRATION, AS URL), and optional parameters such as SECURE, NULL handling, VOLATILE/IMMUTABLE, HEADERS, CONTEXT_HEADERS, MAX_BATCH_ROWS, COMPRESSION, and translators. It also lists access control requirements, usage notes, and a simple example.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the CREATE EXTERNAL FUNCTION command, which calls remote services through a proxy such as API Gateway.
key_facts: CREATE EXTERNAL FUNCTION requires the RETURNS, API_INTEGRATION, and AS clauses; the AS clause specifies the invocation URL of the proxy service and resource.
The API_INTEGRATION parameter names the API integration object used to authenticate the call to the proxy service.
The SECURE keyword hides the URL, HTTP headers, and context headers from all users who are not owners of the function.
The default for NULL handling is NULL, meaning the function can return NULL values.
The default null-input behavior is CALLED ON NULL INPUT; RETURNS NULL ON NULL INPUT (synonym STRICT) skips calling the function when any input is null.
The default volatility is VOLATILE, and Snowflake recommends setting VOLATILE or IMMUTABLE explicitly; IMMUTABLE behavior is not checked or guaranteed by Snowflake.
Snowflake prepends the prefix “sf-custom-” to each name specified in HEADERS before sending them as HTTP headers.
The sum of the sizes of header names and header values for an external function must be less than or equal to 8 KB.
CONTEXT_HEADERS binds supported context functions such as CURRENT_USER() or CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() to HTTP headers prefixed with “sf-context”.
MAX_BATCH_ROWS sets a maximum number of rows per batch sent to the proxy service and is not a performance tuning parameter; Snowflake recommends leaving it unset unless needed.
COMPRESSION valid values are NONE, GZIP, DEFLATE, and AUTO; the default is AUTO, which is GZIP on AWS and NONE on Azure and GCP.
The argument types and the return type cannot be GEOGRAPHY.
Creating an external function requires the CREATE EXTERNAL FUNCTION privilege on the schema, plus USAGE on the parent database and schema, and either OWNERSHIP or USAGE on the API integration.
CREATE OR REPLACE statements are atomic: the old object is deleted and the new object is created in a single transaction.
The example creates local_echo(string_col VARCHAR) returning VARIANT through the API integration demonstration_external_api_integration_01 with an Amazon API Gateway URL.
